title: Library: timings and floors
summary: Timings (Ajanta hall 24×7), floor guide, e-journals, remote access, Book Bank, tips.

posts.md:
The **Central Library** is one of the most frequently used spaces on campus, serving students for studying, research, accessing digital resources, and quiet reading.

The library is a **four-storey building** with:

- Reading Halls for Books, Journals, and References
- Book Bank
- Back volumes in Humanities, Social Sciences, Management, Engineering, Technology, and Science
- Children's Library Corner

### Timings

- **Central Library:** 8:00 AM – 12:00 Midnight (Daily)
- **Ajanta Reading Hall:** **Open 24×7**, making it a popular study space during exam season.

## Floor-by-Floor Guide

## Ground Floor

- Circulation Desk (Book Issue & Return)
- Reference Section
- Administrative Services
- Library Membership Registration
- Book Bank

The **Book Bank** allows eligible students to borrow textbooks for the entire semester.

## First Floor

A spacious and well-ventilated reading hall with:

- Face-to-face seating
- Side tables along the walls
- Bright natural lighting
- Campus views

A great place for focused individual study.

## Second & Third Floors

These floors feature:

- Row-by-row seating
- Bookshelves throughout

The **Third Floor** is one of the most preferred study spaces because it offers:

- Air-conditioned seating
- Good lighting
- Charging ports
- Water coolers
- Nearby washrooms

Seats fill up quickly during exam season, so arriving early is recommended.

## Top Floor

A quieter and more intimate reading room, well suited for **group study sessions**.

## Digital Resources

The IIT Madras Central Library provides access to a wide range of digital resources for coursework and research.

## e-Journals & Databases

Students have access to major academic resources, including:

- IEEE Xplore
- Elsevier ScienceDirect
- Springer
- Wiley
- Nature
- ACM Digital Library

Additionally, IIT Madras is receiving access to **30 additional resources** through the Government of India's **One Nation One Subscription (ONOS)** initiative.

## Remote Access

Subscribed e-resources can be accessed **off-campus** through the IIT Madras remote access portal using IITM login credentials.

This allows students to access research papers and journals from their hostel or anywhere else.

## WEBOPAC

The library's online catalogue allows students to:

- Search books
- Reserve books
- Renew books

without visiting the library.

## Special Resources

The library also provides access to:

- PressReader
- The Ken
- YNOS Venture Engine
- JoVE Journals
- National Digital Library of India

## Institutional Repository (IRePoSe)

The **Institutional Repository (IRePoSe)** hosts:

- Theses
- Research reports
- Research papers by IIT Madras students and faculty

It is a valuable resource for literature reviews and research projects.

## Awards & Recognition

The IIT Madras Central Library has received several recognitions, including:

- **Wiley Library Award 2019** in the **"Digitally Transformed Academic Library (Government)"** category.
- **ISO 9001:2015 Certification** from **TÜV NORD, Germany** for its Quality Management System.

## Tips for Students

- The **Third Floor** is the preferred study space for many students because of its air-conditioning, charging ports, and quiet environment.
- The **Ajanta Reading Hall** is open **24×7**, making it especially useful during end-semester exams.
- Set up **remote access** on your laptop early in the semester to access journals and research databases from anywhere.
- Apply for the **Book Bank** at the beginning of the semester, as registrations are limited and fill up quickly.
